svg.title: Working, episodic, semantic and procedural memory
svg.desc: The four kinds of memory in the CoALA framework, each with the mechanism it corresponds to. At the bottom, working memory: the prompt of the current call, with the instructions, what was retrieved and the conversation so far. Above it, three long-term memories. Episodic: records of past sessions, such as the raw turns or summaries of them. Semantic: facts and knowledge, such as a profile of the user, extracted facts, or a document collection that retrieval-augmented generation reads but never writes. Procedural: how to act, kept in the model's weights, the agent's code, and instructions or skill files. Retrieval brings long-term memory into the prompt; learning writes from the prompt into long-term memory. Memory about a user, the subject of this series, is episodic and semantic; procedural memory is left out.
